Bio |work=UCLABruins.com |url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordan-adams/2772}} is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Dewa United Banten BC|Dewa United Banten]] of the [[Indonesian Basketball League]] (IBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. He was the first UCLA freshman to score 20 or more [[point (basketball)|points]] in his first four games, and was an [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] first-team selection in the [[Pac-12 Conference]] in his sophomore year. After deciding to forgo his remaining college eligibility and enter the [[2014 NBA draft]], Adams was selected by [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the first round with the 22nd overall pick. He played two seasons with Memphis before being waived after multiple knee surgeries. ==Early life== Adams was born in [[Atlanta]] to John Adams, a nutrition manager, and Sabrina Robinson Johnson, a dental hygienist. His parents never married but remained friends. When Adams was in the fourth grade and his life began to revolve around [[American football]] and [[basketball]], he moved from his mother's house to his father's. One of Adams' coaches was usually his father from when he was six until he was 16.{{cite news |last=Dave |first=Paresh |title=UCLA guard Jordan Adams' family goes the extra mile |date=December 6, 2013 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/ucla/la-sp-1207-ucla-jordan-adams-20131207,0,4073485,full.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140422071710/http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/ucla/la-sp-1207-ucla-jordan-adams-20131207,0,4073485,full.story |archive-date=April 22, 2014 |url-status=dead }} Adams attended [[Central Gwinnett High School]] in [[Lawrenceville, Georgia]], for his first two seasons.{{cite web |last1=Foster |first1=Chris |title=C. Gwinnett star Adams is UCLA's 'silent assassin' |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/gwinnett-star-adams-ucla-silent-assassin/OScVg806N5ZWWCpzls9JQL/ |website=Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=September 7, 2023 |date=March 26, 2014}} He transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Virginia]] for his final two seasons, where he was the ninth player in their basketball program's rich history to score 1,000 career points. Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Adams was listed as the No. 9 small forward and the No. 41 player in the nation in 2012.[https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/67412/ Jordan Adams Recruiting Profile] He also played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball with the Atlanta Celtics. Shortly after Celtics' coach Korey McCray became an assistant coach at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), Adams accepted an [[athletic scholarship]] to play for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]].{{cite news |last=Holmes |first=Baxter |title=Unassuming Bruins guard Jordan Adams is first among equals |date=December 8, 2012 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2012-dec-08-la-sp-1208-ucla-jordan-adams-20121208-story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304051806/http://articles.latimes.com/2012/dec/08/sports/la-sp-1208-ucla-jordan-adams-20121208 |archive-date=March 4, 2014 |url-status=live }} ==College career== Adams in 2012 joined fellow incoming freshman [[Shabazz Muhammad]], [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]], and [[Tony Parker (basketball, born 1993)|Tony Parker]] in a UCLA recruiting class considered the best in the nation. The first of the four recruits to sign, Adams was the only one that was not a [[McDonald's All-American]] in high school. Despite the competition, he remained committed to UCLA. He began the [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13 season]] with 20 or more points in the first four games, becoming the first UCLA freshman to accomplish that feat; he was the first Bruin in any class to start the season with four straight since [[Don MacLean (basketball)|Don MacLean]] (6 straight) in [[1990–91 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1990–91]].{{cite web |title=UCLA BASKETBALL – 2012-13 SEASON NOTES |publisher=UCLA Sports Information |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/fls/30500/pdf/MBKB_13SeasonNotes.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30500 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222014200/http://www.uclabruins.com/fls/30500/pdf/MBKB_13SeasonNotes.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=30500 |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |url-status=live }} Though he did not start until the seventh game of the season, Adams was second on the team in scoring behind Muhammad. He finished the season starting in 27 of 33 games played, ranked eighth in the [[Pac-12 Conference]] in scoring with 15.3 points per game, led the conference with 73 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], and was fourth with an 84.3 [[free throw percentage]].{{cite press release |title=No. 4-seed UCLA (26-8) vs. No. 13-seed Tulsa (21-12) |publisher=UCLA Sports Information |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/pdf9/2660851.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140321005304/http://www.uclabruins.com/pdf9/2660851.pdf |archive-date=March 21, 2014 |url-status=dead }} UCLA coach [[Ben Howland]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] coach [[Sean Miller]] were surprised that Adams did not make the conference's all-freshman team. Miller further believed that Adams should have been named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12 team]] as well as the conference's all-defensive team.{{cite news |last=Yoon |first=Peter |title=Howland 'miffed' at Adams all-conference snub |date=March 12, 2013 |work=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/UCLA/post/_/id/13556/howland-miffed-at-adams-all-conference-snub |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224105344/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/UCLA/post/_/id/13556/howland-miffed-at-adams-all-conference-snub |archive-date=February 24, 2014 |url-status=live }} In the semifinals of the [[2013 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2013 Pac-12 tournament]], Adams scored 11 points in the last six minutes in a comeback victory over Arizona. However, he broke his right foot on the final play of the game; he had fractured the same foot in high school. Without Adams, the Bruins lost their next two games, including a season-ending loss to the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers]] in the opener of the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]]. Two days after the season ended, Howland was fired and replaced by [[Steve Alford]]. Adams did not play basketball for four months while his foot healed.
